claims.text: High-temperature solution treatment and quenching can produce a single-phase, disordered BCC state in equimolar NbMoTaW.
Aging near 800°C for 2 hours can induce nanoscale second-phase precipitation in the solutionized refractory high-entropy alloy.
The aging-induced particles may be ordered B2 or Laves-type phases.
The specified aging treatment will produce a uniformly distributed dispersion of nanoscale precipitates.
The nanoscale precipitates pin dislocations and impede dislocation motion.
Dislocation-particle interactions increase strain or work hardening.
Impeded dislocation glide increases yield strength.
Increased work hardening delays plastic instability.
Delayed plastic instability improves uniform plastic strain or ductility.
Compared with the as-solutionized alloy, the aged alloy will have higher yield strength.
Compared with the as-solutionized alloy, the aged alloy will have greater uniform plastic strain or ductility.
The as-solutionized reference alloy has a single-phase BCC structure and lacks aging-induced precipitates.
The proposed strength-plasticity improvement should hold for NbMoTaW and compositionally related refractory high-entropy alloys under the specified aging conditions.
Changing alloy composition, aging temperature, or aging duration can change precipitate morphology or volume fraction.
Changes in precipitate morphology or volume fraction can alter the resulting strength-plasticity response.
